name: Triads

attributes.attribute: list three examples of qualities, people, or places
record the three splendid women of King Arthur's court

sources: Bromwich, Rachel. Trioedd Ynys Prydein: The Welsh Triads. Cardiff: University of Wales Press, 1961.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Triads are a Welsh and Irish literary form. Poets and other bards composed them because of the mystic power of the number three. A triad is a short poem that lists three examples of a quality, a person, or a place. The gain of a triad was easy memory. The Triads of the island of Britain list the three splendid women of King Arthur's court. They also record the three sorrows of Ireland and many other groups. Scholars study the Triads for the myth material they hold.

okr.objective: Record the Welsh and Irish Triads.
